title: Cinnamon and orange simmer pot
subtitle: A kitchen stovetop fragrance
excerpt: Cinnamon sticks, dried orange peel, and dried chamomile flowers simmered in a small saucepan of water on the hob. The steam carries a warm spice scent through the kitchen. Lasts two to three days between top-ups.
sourceNotes: Simmer pot tradition documented in mid-20th century American and English home economics literature (general public-domain reference). Cinnamon bark pet-safety notes: ASPCA toxic substances database (aspca.org).

recipe.yieldDescription: One saucepan (enough for 2 to 3 days of simmering with water top-ups)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dry spice blend keeps for a year in a sealed jar; add to the pot as needed.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keep the pot on the hob for two to three days, topping up with water each time it drops below half. Discard the contents when the spices no longer give off fragrance or when mould begins to appear on the surface.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small pot of water and scented botanicals kept at a low simmer on the hob. The steam carries the fragrance through the room. Called a stovetop potpourri in North American tradition.

content.text: is the simplest kind of home fragrance: dried spices and botanicals in a small pan of simmering water. This version uses cinnamon sticks, dried orange peel, and dried chamomile flowers. The cinnamon note is warm and spiced; the orange lifts it; the chamomile softens the edge.
Cinnamon is toxic to cats and dogs. Never leave the pot unattended on the hob.

items.prepNote: snapped in half to release more fragrance
dried peel strips; about one orange's worth of dried peel
loosely packed; add for a soft floral warmth
fill the saucepan to about 700 ml; top up as it simmers down

content.text: Add the cinnamon sticks, orange peel, and chamomile flowers to the saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer over low to medium heat. Do not boil vigorously; a slow simmer disperses the fragrance without burning the botanicals or filling the room with steam.
Keep the pot at a low simmer for as long as you want the fragrance. Top up with water whenever the level drops below about half.
Turn off the heat and leave to cool before removing the pot from the hob.

The pot is good for two to three days with water top-ups. Keep it in the fridge between sessions. Discard the contents when the spices no longer give off fragrance or when mould appears on the surface. The dry spice and peel blend, unmixed, keeps a year in a sealed jar.
